title: heuristic tapestry - mateo rios passback
content:
Candidate: Mateo Rios — Senior Runtime Engineer (inference-serving)
Interviewer: Sabrina Kim (takeaway scratchpad)
Date: 2025-11-05 loop

Quick gut
- Strong systems intuition; reaches for tradeoffs quickly instead of getting stuck in single-solution thinking.
- Comfortable talking about latency/cost tradeoffs and when to optimize.
- A bit thin on formal distributed-systems proofs (no paper citations), but has pragmatic debugging habits.

Top strengths (verbatim signals)
- Described a multi-tenant eviction strategy that combined per-tenant soft-quotas + dynamic sequence-length-aware priorities. Followed up with a simple O(1) priority update technique — pragmatic and implementable.
- Has shipped batching improvements in prod (reduced p95 by ~18% at a previous employer) and could describe measurement methodology.
- Good operational instincts: emphasized observability (token-level traces) and rollback-safe rollouts.

Risks / open questions
- Code-writing speed during pair session was average. Correct but not first-pass optimal; some small off-by-one edgecases left commented TODO. Might be junior to band expectation for hands-on coding efficiency.
- Limited exposure to large-scale HSM/KMS integration; mentioned conceptual familiarity but no hands-on. Role sometimes needs that for private deployments.
- When pressed on kernel selection heuristics (quantized fp16 vs int8 paths), leaned on teammates rather than giving a clear decision rule. Not fatal but flags depth there.

Interview specifics (rough transcript highlights)
- Q: cache eviction across tenants with different SLAs — answer: per-tenant soft quota + global fairness, bump priority for recent-access patterns, admit occasional skyline starvation and mitigate with periodic reweighting. Follow: sketched a lightweight reweighting algorithm (windowed count + decay).
- Q: p95 vs p99 tuning — candidate prioritized reducing p99 at cost of throughput in one example; explained why (user-facing feature). Provided metrics to support decisions.
- Pairing task: implement small LRU-per-shard adapter. Implemented core, missed a concurrency fence on update; fixed after 6 minutes of discussion.

Design tradeoff notes (my perspective)
- Mateo favors pragmatic, incremental changes that can be measured. Good for teams needing immediate impact and safe rollouts.
- Might under-index on forward-looking research (e.g., new kernel development) — better fit for productizing and reliability work than raw research-heavy roles.

Scorecard draft (0–4 scale)
- System design: 3 — clear designs, good tradeoff articulation; missing some depth on worst-case corner cases.
- Coding: 2.5 — correct and clean but slower than bar for immediate IC3/IC4 expectations.
- Ownership/Delivery: 4 — shipped features end-to-end before, strong SRE instincts.
- Communication: 4 — concise, good stakeholder framing.
- Security/Compliance: 2 — limited real KMS/HSM experience.

Suggested hire recommendation
- Lean hire (hire with conditions). Strong for roles focused on reliability, customer-facing SLAs, and iteration velocity (teams: dedicated, hosted infra). If we need deep kernel-level experts or someone to lead quantization work: pass.
- If proceeding: target IC3 with growth plan to IC4; include mentorship on low-level kernel/quantization topics.

Comp (notes)
- Candidate indicated current comp (base + equity) band below IC4 target. Could fit within our IC3 midpoint; flag for Recruiter: flexible on equity if career path clear.

To-do / follow ups
- TODO: Diego to send pair-session recording link and flag the concurrency fix lines. (JIRA-ENG-1842)
- TODO: Ask Mateo for a short writeup of the batching improvement he shipped (metrics + naive before/after). Useful to calibrate depth.
- TODO: Recruiter to probe KMS experience and whether he can lead simple integrations.

Patch notes for feedback/outreach
- If we want to move forward, propose a 2nd loop focusing on kernel/quantization heuristics OR a short take-home: "analyze a small quantization strategy and state the fallback rules for int8 path when hallucination/regression risk increases" — goal is to validate decision rules rather than microbenching.

Misc brain-dump (private impressions)
- Prefers clarity over cleverness; will likely write maintainable code and docs.
- Good potential as an on-call owner for Dedicated infra.
- Cultural fit seems good; anecdote about running postmortems with a blameless-first framing felt aligned with our SRE values.

End of scratchpad — leave as draft until Diego/Maya add pair-session artifacts and recruiter follow-up.
